etymologies.etymologyHTML: First attested in 1620–1630. Borrowed from French cooperation, from Late Latin cooperātiō. By surface analysis, co- +‎ operation.

definitions.definition: Active help from a person, organization, etc., such as an orderly sharing of space or resources.

quote.text:
South Korea is seeking cooperation from China to produce artificial rain to help fight increasing pollution.
Audio (US):(file)

definitions.definition: Association for mutual benefit, such as for purposes of production or purchase.
